direct_answer: Yes. MOTOR OIL Group discloses that “Decarbonization and Energy Transition is the foundation of the … strategic plan” and presents an “ambitious Energy Transition plan” with a net-zero goal by 2050 and interim 2030 targets (Scope 1&2: -30% vs 2021; Scope 3: -25% vs 2021) as part of its transition plan for climate change mitigation [Source 1]. Regarding 1.5°C alignment, the report states that the Group is “formulating a climate transition plan aligned with the 1.5℃ target” [Source 9] and that its scenario analysis includes scenarios “consistent with a 1.5℃ global warming trajectory” [Source 2], including a “Net Zero scenario… consistent with limiting the global temperature rise to 1.5-2.0℃” [Source 3]. However, the retrieved passages do not provide the ESRS E1-1/E1-4-required explanation of how the Group’s specific GHG targets are compatible with limiting warming to 1.5°C (e.g., science-based framework/methodology, underlying scenarios used to set targets, and external assurance of targets) [Sources 1, 2, 3, 9]. Therefore, based on the provided excerpts, 1.5°C alignment is asserted but not fully substantiated.
compliance_rationale: Evidence shows the undertaking has a transition plan and discloses net-zero by 2050 plus 2030 Scope 1&2 and Scope 3 reduction targets [Source 1]. Evidence also shows an explicit claim of alignment with a 1.5°C target and use of 1.5°C-consistent scenario analysis [Sources 2, 3, 9]. But the retrieved passages do not include the detailed ESRS E1-1.16(a)/E1-4.34(e) elements needed to demonstrate target compatibility with 1.5°C (e.g., science-based methodology/framework, scenario assumptions used to set targets, and whether targets are externally assured).
disclosure_gaps: Explicit explanation of how the disclosed 2030/2050 GHG targets are compatible with limiting warming to 1.5°C (beyond a general statement of alignment) (ESRS E1-1.16(a)) [Sources 1, 9].
Whether and how the GHG targets are science-based, including the framework/methodology used (e.g., SBTi or other) (ESRS E1-4.34(e)) — not evidenced in retrieved passages [Sources 1, 2, 3, 9].
Underlying climate and policy scenarios used specifically to set the targets (not just for resilience/scenario analysis) (ESRS E1-4.34(e)) [Sources 2, 3].
Whether the GHG targets have been externally assured (ESRS E1-4.34(e)) — not evidenced in retrieved passages [Sources 1, 11].
key_findings: Transition plan exists and is positioned as central to strategy; includes net-zero by 2050 and 2030 targets (Scope 1&2: -30%; Scope 3: -25%; baseline 2021) [Source 1].
The company states it is formulating a climate transition plan aligned with the 1.5°C target [Source 9].
Scenario analysis includes a 1.5°C-consistent trajectory and a net-zero scenario consistent with 1.5–2.0°C [Sources 2, 3].
